transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Stop using the machine immediately. Once the machine is safely isolated, I can help you understand what might be causing the leak. Common causes include a loose drain hose at the back, a failed pump seal, or an internal hose coming loose. However, because water has reached the electrical point, this requires professional inspection before any further use.

ok the fuse box is in the hall and the floor there is dry, so I can get to it. I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now though, should I get off it first? the water has definitely run back towards the plug

Yes, get off the wet floor immediately. Socks are not insulated against electricity. Because water has reached the electrical plug point, this appliance must not be used again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has inspected both the machine's internal wiring/pump and your kitchen socket. Water in an electrical connection can cause short circuits or fire hazards that are not visible from the outside. The primary issue now is safety: stop using the machine until it has been professionally inspected.
